| Scene description | • S06-A is in Luguang Community, Hongshan District.<br>• S06-A-01: of three green roadside bins, the left overflows with white foam containers and bags and bears black graffiti; the others do not overflow but have stained interiors.<br>• S06-A-02: red, gray, green, and black bins stand by a sorting board. Cardboard and waste are visible in the red bin; other bins do not overflow, although paper accumulates inside the green one.<br>• S06-A-04: a non-overflowing green cylindrical bin with a white label and black liner stands by pavement and electric bicycles.<br>• S06-A-05: green roadside bins include an overflowing food-waste bin with leaves, paper cups, and bags; leaves and paper lie nearby. Another bin does not overflow and the remainder are normal. Some green bins are old or dirty, amid vehicles, electric bicycles, and shops. |
| Regulatory basis | • Residential provision should cover all four categories, with food/other-waste containers in a 1:1–1:3 ratio. Enclosed communities need at least one hazardous-waste and one recyclables point; open areas need these per 300–500 households. Food/other-waste bins should adjoin building entrances, integrated recyclables/other-waste bins leisure areas, and hazardous-waste/recyclables containers main entrances and passages. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4 (clause ID [D-16-C004](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Containers must remain intact and functional; continued non-compliance after a correction deadline incurs CNY 1,000–3,000 for organizations. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (1) (clause ID [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Improper storage or transfer requires correction; continued non-compliance incurs CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (2) (clause ID [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Failure to sort at designated locations requires correction; refusal incurs CNY 50,000–500,000 for organizations or CNY 100–1,000 for individuals. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (3) (clause ID [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Mixing sorted waste during collection or transport requires correction; continued non-compliance incurs CNY 5,000–30,000 for collectors. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (4) (clause ID [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Non-compliant treatment requires correction; continued non-compliance incurs CNY 30,000–50,000 for treatment organizations and compensation for losses. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (5) (clause ID [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Waste enterprises failing duties require correction and may incur CNY 5,000–30,000 for sweeping, collection, or transport and CNY 30,000–100,000 for treatment. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 45 (clause ID [D-03-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering, or stockpiling requires cessation and correction, with CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations or up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42 (clause ID [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Daily removal and progressive separate disposal, collection, and transport are required. Refusal to correct prescribed disposal practices incurs CNY 100–1,000 for individuals or CNY 50,000–500,000 for organizations. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 29 (clause ID [D-06-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)).<br>• Disposal points should be clean without retained waste, wastewater, or secondary pollution; containers require orderly provision, clear labels, inspections, prompt emptying, washing, disinfection, and repair or replacement. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4 Maintenance requirements (clause ID [D-16-C009](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv)). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Three overflows and two accumulations, concentrated in food-waste bins with some old or dirty containers, impair residential conditions and pose secondary pollution and sanitation risks without extensive litter or severe pollution. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: spillage scatters leaves and paper; dirty bins pose odor and vector risks. Possible short-term impacts: delays may increase complaints, harm community reputation, breed vectors, and obstruct pedestrian movement or parking. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** insufficient collections or failure of daily removal. Mixed waste overflows from S06-A-05, with litter and no visible collectors or vehicles.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** incorrect sorting, including paper in the S06-A-02 green bin and bags or paper cups in the S06-A-05 food-waste bin.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** inadequate provision or maintenance. Old, dirty green bins at S06-A-01, S06-A-04, and S06-A-05 lack visible other categories; S06-A-02 has four colors but may not be a fixed point.<br>- **Verification:** inspect collection records and inventories, four-category provision, and regular inspections, washing, and repairs. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, trust and disposal behavior may worsen; waste may breed insects and rodents and increase health risks; residential quality and community image may decline; and fines may apply to managers or individuals under Article 18(1) and (3) of the Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification. |
| Recommendations | **Immediate actions:** empty overflow and accumulations, clear litter, wash and disinfect bins and ground, repair or replace dirty or damaged bins, add hazardous-waste and recyclables containers at S06-A-01, S06-A-04, and S06-A-05 to complete four-category provision, and post sorting guidance.<br>**Long-term measures:** inspect regularly to keep overflow below 10%; ensure daily food-waste removal; train community managers in duties and liability; introduce smart sorting equipment or sorting supervisors. |
| Priority | **High.** Multiple overflows and accumulations, including mixed waste spilling from food-waste bins, create clear sanitation and secondary pollution risks affecting residents and potentially triggering penalties. Immediate action is needed. |
